inputs.wacc_rationale: RMB flows discounted at an RMB-built rate. China 10y CGB ~1.8% + beta ~0.95 x China ERP ~6.5% = ~8.0% CoE, +1pp for an HK-listed state-controlled subsidiary with related-party cash placements (governance/capital-allocation, not cyclicality -- cyclicality is in the bear-weighted scenarios). Net cash, so WACC = CoE = 9.0%, identical across scenarios (risk charged once). Terminal growth 1.5% reflects low RMB inflation and a volume-flat domestic fertilizer market.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities (32.7 at 30-Jun-2026) are immaterial and deducted once in equity_bridge; no lease charge in the flows (lease_cost_pct 0).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are whole-group (EBITDA is consolidated); NCI is charged once by deducting its book value (217.6) in equity_bridge. NCI profit share is ~1% of group profit, so book is a fair proxy.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF with cyclical adaptations (routing row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical'). Sinofert is a Sinochem-controlled fertilizer distributor (potash import/strategic reserve, compound, phosphate, nitrogen) with some own production (Sinochem Fuling, Changshan etc.) -- an operating business, not a holdco or financial. EBITDA basis: the CSV's EBITDA = profit from operations + depreciation (FY2025 1,498.0 + 444.1 = 1,942.1); share of JV/associate results sits below that line and is excluded from flows, with the JV/associate stakes added at book in the bridge. Interest income (134.6 FY2025) sits inside 'other income and gains' and therefore inside reported EBITDA; it is stripped from the margin path (FY2025 EBITDA ex-interest 1,807.5 = 7.77% of revenue) and the cash that earns it is in net cash. H1 FY2026 profit from operations 1,563 includes a 148.7 one-off reversal of impairment on financial assets, excluded from the FY2026 margin judgment. Margins on the ex-interest basis: FY18 2.9%, FY19 4.1%, FY20 3.4%, FY21 3.8%, FY22 5.4%, FY23 5.8%, FY24 6.4%, FY25 7.8% -- FY2025 is the high of the series, so the base case glides it back to a 6.3% mid-cycle (below the FY23-25 mean of 6.7%). SBC zero: house and street coincide, band_position null. No buybacks: flat count is the actual history, not a funded convention. H1 seasonality: operating cash flow negative in H1 every year as farmer prepayments unwind; this is not modelled as a trend.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (7.0%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue 5yr CAGR (1.7%). Book growth is retained earnings from a margin expansion (3.4% -> 7.8% ex-interest EBITDA margin FY20-25) on flat revenue, not volume growth; capitalising 7% would extrapolate a margin re-rating that is already at the top of its range. Revenue CAGR selected instead. FCF CAGRs (owner basis, reported FCF less interest income; SBC zero) are dominated by working-capital swings off a low FY2020 base (239) and are not a usable growth signal.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - interest income (SBC 0): FY2020 239.4, FY2022 750.5, FY2025 1,569.6. FY2017 (loss of RMB2.2bn, negative FCF) is outside the 5yr window but is the reminder that this series has had a loss year.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +6% (H1 +10.6% on potash volume and price; H2 is the small half), then volume-flat China fertilizer demand at ~2% nominal. Ex-interest EBITDA margin 7.4% in FY2026 (H1 ex the 149m impairment reversal ran ahead of H1 FY2025), gliding to a 6.3% mid-cycle by FY2030. Cash tax rises from ~18% effective (HNTE 15% subsidiaries, utilised losses) to 22%. Capex 2.2% of revenue, above 1.9% depreciation, matching the FY18-25 average net of the FY21-22 plant build. Working capital consumes 5% of incremental revenue (inventory net of farmer prepayments).

bull.narrative: The FY2022-25 margin step-up is structural: potash import-contract and strategic-reserve role, specialty/bio and new-type fertilizers and own-production mix hold ex-interest EBITDA near 7.5%; revenue grows 2.5-4% on specialty volume.

bear.narrative: Fertilizer down-cycle: potash contract price resets lower, export controls keep domestic nitrogen/phosphate oversupplied, and distribution margin reverts to the FY2019-21 range (~4% ex-interest); revenue dips 5% then grows only with inflation.

scenario_narratives.base: Sinofert's earnings are a distribution spread on potash, compound, phosphate and nitrogen fertilizer plus some own-plant production, set largely by China's annual potash import contract price, domestic oversupply under export controls, and grain-price-driven farmer demand. Base assumes FY2026 is another good year (H1 profit +7%, revenue +10.6%) and the margin then reverts toward a 6.3% mid-cycle -- below the FY2023-25 average -- on a flat-volume market.
scenario_narratives.bull: The post-2018 restructuring (exit of loss-making units, potash channel scale, biological/specialty products, Sinochem group procurement leverage) made the 7-8% margin the new normal, and revenue compounds 3% on specialty and new-type fertilizers.
scenario_narratives.bear: The margin expansion was cyclical: potash prices and the strategic-reserve release spread normalise, domestic competition intensifies as export space narrows (management already flags 'compressing industry profit margins'), and margin falls back to the 4% of FY2019-21 while revenue shrinks. FY2017's RMB2.2bn impairment-driven loss shows tail risk beyond even this case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (above the 15% default): FY2025 is the highest margin in the series and the business is a commodity spread with a loss year in recent memory. Base 50%: mid-cycle reversion is the central expectation. Bull 20% (below default): it requires the whole 2022-25 margin step to be structural in a market management itself describes as margin-compressing.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Cyclical, SBC-zero, net-cash state-linked distributor valued on mid-cycle owner FCF in RMB at an RMB cost of equity, converted to HKD. Net cash is taken at the seasonal June low and interest income is stripped from EBITDA so the cash is counted once. The market prices the stock at roughly 2x EV/EBITDA and ~6x earnings, i.e. it gives little credit for either the cash or the earnings -- a classic HK SOE-subsidiary discount; the gap to intrinsic value is a re-rating/cash-access thesis, not a growth thesis.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cash access: a large share of time deposits sits with a Sinochem fellow subsidiary; the value of net cash to minorities depends on payout policy (FY2025 dividends 525m, ~42% payout).
Cyclicality: potash contract price and domestic fertilizer spreads; FY2017 RMB2.2bn loss.
Policy: export controls/quotas on urea and phosphate, strategic-reserve obligations, fertilizer price guidance.
Chronically low multiple: no re-rate means the market value tracks cash plus a few years of earnings, not DCF value.
Working-capital seasonality: H1 operating cash flow is negative every year; year-end cash includes farmer prepayments.
